# Temple Scroll Column 30 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 30 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 30:3 — "equidistant from each other" vs. "spaced at equal intervals" vs. "equally spaced"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "equidistant from each other and from the corners" | Uses technical measurement term |
| LOGOS | "spaced at equal intervals from one another and from the corners" | More descriptive phrasing |
| PNEUMA | "equally spaced from each other and from the corners" | Simple, clear |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's simplified form: "equally spaced from one another and from the corners." Clear and concise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA (with slight adjustment).

---

## 30:5 — "porch" vs. "portico" vs. "entrance hall" / "towers" vs. "watchtowers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "porch... towers" | Simple English terms |
| LOGOS | "portico... towers" | Classical architectural vocabulary |
| PNEUMA | "entrance hall... watchtowers" | Descriptive modern terms specifying function |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "porch... towers." "Porch" is consistent with Column 26/28 renderings. "Towers" is accurate without PNEUMA's speculative addition of "watch-" function.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 30:9 — "same measurements" vs. "same dimensions" vs. "match the same dimensions"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the same measurements" | Literal phrasing |
| LOGOS | "conform to the same dimensions" | Formal register |
| PNEUMA | "match the same dimensions" | Active verb form |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted a simplified form: "the same dimensions." "Dimensions" is slightly more precise than "measurements" for architectural specifications, without LOGOS's formal "conform to."

**Status:** Resolved with composite.

---

## 30:15 — "a square from corner to corner" with or without editorial comment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a square from corner to corner" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "forming a square from corner to corner" | Adds participial construction |
| PNEUMA | "a massive square measured from corner to corner" | Adds "massive" editorial comment |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "a square from corner to corner." The text should describe without editorializing. "Massive" (PNEUMA) is interpretive commentary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 30:16 — "hewn stone" vs. "dressed stone" vs. "cut stone"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hewn stone" | Traditional biblical English for even gazit |
| LOGOS | "dressed stone" | Technical masonry term |
| PNEUMA | "cut stone" | Simple modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "hewn stone." This is the traditional and established English rendering of even gazit in biblical translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
